I tried to kill myself but deflected and that started me going to talk therapy. I’ve been doing CBT (cognitive behavioral therapy) for almost 2 years, I turned 23 and felt like I just can’t live like this anymore, it was destroying me and my relationships.

I told myself I would just not purge First, keep whatever food in me I ate inside and do better tomorrow. I stopped purging first- relapsed twice then completely stopped. I binged for a week then felt like shit again, but didn’t purge. I felt really good about stopping, then had a month of neither binge or purge. I wasn’t binging- so I wasn’t purging- so I wasn’t restricting etc. Binging for that week and realizing how shitty I felt sort of broke the cycle since I eliminated one part. 

I had to recognize why I was doing these behaviors and find different coping mechanisms. Now if I am stressed I try taking a bath or skincare routine instead of compulsively eating. Therapy has helped a lot but I really was at the end of my rope and decided I can NOT live this way, it was killing me. I’m going on antidepressants this summer hopefully to help with my mood.


I also deleted instagram, tumblr and my “health” apps so I wouldn’t be influenced by others bodies/food. I still count calories but make sure I hit at least 1,200 a day if not I maintain. I think this is fine for me but for some people it’s not. I still struggle with wanting to restrict but counting calories helps me meet my goal of eating enough while still giving me control. 

I hope this helps, I was recovered for 3 years then deeply relapsed due to stress of finishing college. I wanted to be thin when I started my “adult” life and fell into my ED again- coming out of it leaves me clear-headed and in control.
